decision: routed to figure-it-out, not the Feature playbook
why: ambitious multi-part build, two one-way-door decisions, and a correctness claim that needs a real gate
result: rigor set high

decision: Next.js 16.4.3 + React 19.3 + Tailwind 4, TypeScript, App Router, src dir
why: CLAUDE.md mandates Next.js App Router with Tailwind for websites
result: scaffolded, deps installed

decision: sent the 3.4MB bundled Next 16 docs to a subagent instead of reading them here
why: Next's own AGENTS.md says this version breaks from older training data, but the docs would eat the context window
result: agent running

decision: scope grew mid-turn to rockets, asteroids, N-body gravity, time control and an AI layer
why: user sent three follow-ups before any engine code existed, which is the cheapest moment to absorb them
result: reframed, 11 predicates

decision: physics engine will be pure TypeScript, no DOM and no WebGL
why: same code then runs in the browser, in a worker, and in a Node route handler, so the AI tools and the CI gates hit the real engine
result: settled before any rendering code

decision: AI gets tools that call the engine, and is never the source of a number
why: a narrated figure the engine did not compute is the failure mode that would make an engineer dismiss the whole thing
result: gate planned

decision: removed cacheComponents and partialPrefetching from next.config
why: the bundled docs say cacheComponents keeps routes mounted as hidden Activity, which leaks a WebGL context
result: typecheck passes

decision: branded units at the data boundary, bare SI inside the engine
why: NASA sources mix au, km, degrees and days, and a silent factor-of-1000 error still draws a pretty orbit
result: typecheck passes

decision: typecheck script runs next typegen before tsc
why: tsc alone fails on the generated LayoutProps type, which cost one confusing error already
result: verified, exit 0

decision: measured the real numeric kernels instead of guessing whether we need Rust or C++
why: the user asked if this should be a lower level language, and that is a timing question, not a preference
result: no rewrite needed, see next rows

decision: limiter is the Kepler solve transcendentals, not the gravity sum
why: RK4 with planet positions recomputed runs 2.74e5 steps/s, with them frozen 5.54e6, a 20x gap, and the gravity sum is 1.2 percent of a step
result: limiter named and mapped to source

decision: decided against a lower level language and against a desktop app
why: the 20x win is algorithmic via interpolated perturber positions, bigger than the 2-5x a WASM port buys, and a URL reaches more people than an installer
result: decided, stated to user

decision: Horizons is server-side only, Standish and IAU tables get embedded
why: JPL states you may not embed their APIs in a website, and Horizons sends no CORS header, confirmed by curl
result: architecture settled

decision: fetched 64 Horizons samples as fixtures before writing the propagator
why: the harness has to exist before the thing it measures, or the tolerance gets chosen to fit the result
result: all returned Ecliptic of J2000.0, script asserts single frame

decision: gate asserts against JPL's own published error bars, not a tolerance we pick
why: a tolerance we choose can be widened until the test passes, which proves nothing
result: delegated, agent running

decision: wrote the user's pasted API key to .env.local and verified it with a live Opus 5 call
why: needed to know the key works before building anything on it
result: verified, KEY OK

decision: measured Mercury's relativistic perihelion advance differentially rather than absolutely
why: RK4 is not symplectic so it precesses on its own, and running both arms identically cancels that
result: 42.9809 vs 42.9807 closed form, 0.001 percent

decision: first run of the relativity gate returned NaN and found a real bug
why: perihelion interpolation seeded rPrev at Infinity and the start point is a perihelion, so shift was Infinity over Infinity
result: fixed, gate green

decision: demonstration registry is the single list and the gate derives from it
why: a separate list of what to test would go stale the first time someone added a demonstration
result: 4 demonstrations, 5 tests green

decision: stopped quoting a recovered planet mass where the elements cannot resolve it
why: Mars printed 11595 percent, which reads as a broken simulation rather than as a precision limit
result: now quotes Jupiter and Saturn only

decision: restructured the ephemeris gate to RMS plus a declared per-body ceiling
why: JPL publishes nominal errors, not bounds, so asserting every epoch inside them failed a correct implementation
result: 17 ephemeris tests green, no tolerance quietly widened

decision: Neptune is 31 arcsec RMS against a 10 arcsec nominal and that is a real limit, not a bug
why: an independent second implementation reproduced the residuals to three decimals and perturbing eccentricity made both channels worse
result: declared and surfaced, will show in the UI

decision: each body gets one contract and a gate that checks it against its own physics
why: the user asked for a per-planet contract, and a contract nothing verifies is a comment
result: green, 2 real source conflicts declared

decision: chose centralized Viewport ownership for the render core
why: two design runners on different models independently picked it and rejected the decentralized shape on the same ground, split ownership of transform writes
result: design settled

decision: eslint zone rule silently did nothing until a planted violation exposed it
why: flat config resolves a rule by last match not union, so the second block disabled the first
result: both fences verified firing

decision: Atlas V is the ascent gate vehicle, not Falcon 9
why: ULA publishes stage masses, engine data and a payload against a defined orbit; SpaceX publishes no stage masses and no reference orbit
result: fixtures captured

decision: first screenshots read as black and the probe agreed, but the probe was broken
why: reading a WebGL canvas through a 2D context returns black without preserveDrawingBuffer; the 260KB PNGs proved content existed
result: measurement moved onto the screenshot bytes

decision: bodies stayed at identity because matrixWorldNeedsUpdate was never set
why: with matrixAutoUpdate off three recomposes matrixWorld once and never again
result: fixed

decision: projection dropped the view matrix translation column, so focus distance was always zero
why: that drove near to its floor and clamped far to 5000km with the camera 38000km out
result: fixed, all 7 shots show bodies

decision: lost four research agents mid-run to a monthly spend limit
why: the Lambert, porkchop and engine-data briefs died at the API and their findings were never written down
result: needs redoing, logged rather than left silent

decision: cross-model review found the eslint conversion fence had a hole and I had only tested the alias spelling
why: a rule that depends on how someone spells a path does not enforce an architecture
result: replaced with a source scan, hole demonstrated and closed

decision: Neptune justification rested on a prior agent's report rather than on anything in the repo
why: the reviewer was right that an unverifiable reason for a widened tolerance is worthless
result: replaced with an in-repo VSOP87 cross-check, which also weakened the Neptune claim

decision: superseding the earlier design row, whose evidence pointer did not resolve
why: it cited PLAYBOOK.md, which never mentioned the two design runs
result: synthesis written down

decision: adaptive Dormand-Prince rather than fixed-step RK4 for small bodies
why: a close encounter needs a tiny step and the quiet stretches do not, and a fixed step pays the worst case everywhere
result: 9 gates green

decision: propagator independently reproduces Einstein's perihelion advance at 0.00 percent error
why: it links the new integrator to a result already gated against the published value, so neither can drift unnoticed
result: 42.981 vs 42.981 arcsec per century

decision: propagation runs in a Web Worker using the unmodified engine function
why: the engine purity decision taken on day one is what made this a zero-change move rather than a port
result: 8590 steps in 192ms, verified in browser

decision: gated impact energy against Chelyabinsk, Tunguska and Chicxulub
why: the formula is easy to get wrong by a factor of a thousand and still look plausible
result: all three inside published yield ranges

decision: committed a red tree while reporting it green, twice, by reading a pipeline's exit code
why: grep and tail return zero even when the command they are piped from failed
result: one check command with pipefail, so the mistake cannot recur

decision: AI gets tools over the engine and is forbidden from producing a number
why: a model asked to integrate an orbit returns a fluent wrong figure and the failure is invisible
result: P11 enforced, verified against the live API

decision: vitest could not resolve the @ alias so a whole test file read as having no tests
why: that failure mode looks identical to an empty passing suite, which is the dangerous kind
result: alias added, 16 tests appeared

decision: inverted the payload gate to solve for implied losses instead of predicting payload
why: predicting payload needs loss precision the literature does not have, and calibrating on Atlas V then predicting Atlas V is circular
result: implied losses 2654 and 2772 m/s, inside the 2 to 3 km/s band

decision: excluded the Atlas V 551 rather than ship a fitted booster model
why: the AJ-60A published figures need 117 percent of the booster mass to be propellant, so any model would be fitted not derived
result: excluded with a test asserting the reason stays stated

decision: a gate caught my energy term making a 2000km orbit cheaper than a 200km one
why: circular speed falls with altitude faster than my separate potential term rose
result: replaced with a full Hohmann from the surface

decision: determined the LOLA byte order by reading the file rather than trusting the spec
why: big-endian gave exactly plus or minus 16384, a power of two, which is byte-swapped noise
result: little-endian, elevation range matches published to within 50 m

decision: PickLayer overlay was swallowing every pointer event so the mouse could not orbit or zoom
why: an absolutely positioned div over a canvas that needs pointer events, only visible when you try to drive it
result: listener moved onto the canvas, zoom verified working

decision: measured where craters actually resolve instead of claiming they do
why: relief peaks at 2000km and collapses below 1000km, which is the data running out not the renderer
result: peak contrast 12.8, limit stated in the UI

decision: derived moon orbital periods from IAU rotation rates rather than quoting them
why: tidal locking makes them identical, and the derived values reproduce published semi-major axes through Kepler to 0.2 percent
result: 9 moons, 217 gates green

decision: two of my pole assumptions were wrong and the corrections became the tests
why: Earth's Moon follows the ecliptic not Earth's equator, and Triton's capture shows in its rotation sign not its pole
result: both now asserted as the real facts

decision: generated 22 moon contracts from fetched JPL and NAIF data rather than typing them
why: transcribing that many numbers is how a wrong element gets in and renders as a plausible orbit
result: 32 bodies, 675 gates green

decision: implemented the warped Laplace plane instead of pinning every moon to its parent's equator
why: Saturn's Laplace radius is 2.5 million km, so Iapetus and Phoebe would have been visibly wrong
result: Rhea 27.8 deg, Iapetus 8.6, Phoebe 4.8, the transition visible

decision: JPL's period column is not the sidereal period for Io and Europa
why: it lists Europa as exactly twice Io, imposing the resonance; the IAU rate fits Kepler better and wins
result: conflict declared on both contracts

decision: integrated the planets mutually in a barycentric frame, not a heliocentric one
why: a pinned Sun makes total momentum non-conserved, throwing away the best free check on the integrator
result: energy drift 1.6e-14, angular momentum 3.6e-14, barycentre 0.85 mm over 100 years

decision: found a frame-conversion bug from the shape of the residual, not from the code
why: four outer planets diverged by the same absolute 491,000 km at 5 to 30 au; equal length at unequal distance is a translation
result: Standish velocities are heliocentric; V_sun needs dividing by total mu and adding to every planet. Jupiter alone is 12.5 m/s, 395,000 km per year

decision: rejected N-body versus Standish as the measurement of mutual perturbation
why: decomposed the residual: it is almost all along-track, which is Standish's own fit error in the initial semi-major axis, not physics
result: replaced by a differential measurement; the Jupiter-Saturn residual came out anti-parallel at 175 deg, which is the great inequality and real

decision: cross-checked the precession against orbit-averaged secular theory written for the purpose
why: one algorithm agreeing with itself is not evidence; the quadrature shares no code and almost no method with Cartesian integration
result: agrees with the integrator to 0.027, 0.003 and 0.009 percent for Venus, Earth and Jupiter

decision: derived the small-alpha closed form by hand so the chain ends at algebra, not at another numerical method
why: Legendre expansion: the l=1 direct term cancels the indirect term, <P2>=1/4, <r^2>=a^2(1+3e^2/2)
result: quadrature converges onto (3/4)sqrt(1-e^2) n (m2/M) alpha^3 to 1.0000 as alpha shrinks

decision: traced a uniform 1 percent precession deficit to a definition, not a missing body
why: a uniform ratio across seven perturbers of different mass and distance cannot be an omission, it has to be a scale factor
result: varpi = Omega + omega, not atan2(e_y,e_x); Mercury's 7 deg inclination makes the gap 2.6 arcsec/cy and Earth's share then lands at 90.08 against a recalled 90.0

decision: declared the published Mercury figure as unverified data rather than asserting it tightly
why: my recalled perihelion budget does not sum self-consistently, so at least one number in my memory is wrong, and the web search budget was exhausted
result: measured 528.9 against a recalled 531.5; gated at 2 percent with the gap stated as unresolved, and the gate forbids tightening it

decision: measured the cost of including moons instead of assuming it
why: a global adaptive step is set by the fastest body, and Phobos orbits in 7.65 hours
result: planets 3.7 s per simulated century; all 32 bodies 950 s, mean step 66 s. Moons offered, cost stated, planets the default

decision: made the tracker report lag rather than drop frames or widen its step
why: at a high time rate a frame can ask for more simulated time than it can afford, and rendering stale positions as live ones is the dishonest failure
result: verified live: zero lag at 120 days per second, 3357 days of admitted lag at 200 years per second

decision: replaced the AI tool gate's hardcoded engine file list with a tree walk
why: the list went stale the moment a tool was backed by a new module, and the obvious fix is to widen it while the real fix is to stop keeping one
result: now requires an actual export, so a backedBy naming a non-existent function still fails

decision: found the differential influence is strongly epoch dependent and stopped asserting a ranking
why: Jupiter's 10-year displacement of Saturn is 19,502 Mm from J2000 and 1,746 Mm from 2026, an 11x swing
result: that is the 900-year Jupiter-Saturn great inequality's phase; the gate now asserts giants beat terrestrials, which is invariant

decision: put what the clock rate means for the focused body on screen next to the period
why: a user read Earth spinning once a second as a bug; 1 day/s is accurate and still does not say you are watching 86,400x real time
result: verified at three rates: 1 day/s gives 1.00 s per turn and 6.1 min per orbit, real time gives 23.9 h and 365.3 days

decision: rendered the night map through onBeforeCompile instead of as an emissiveMap
why: three adds an emissiveMap unconditionally, which would paint city lights across the daylit hemisphere too
result: mask comes from dot(worldNormal, sunDirection); night brightness 12.2 to 20.2, cities visible across Asia and Australia

decision: three silent failure modes in one feature, each found by measurement not by reading
why: a null sampler uniform, a shared program cache entry, and adding after tone mapping all render as no lights and raise no error
result: intercepted shaderSource to prove the injection compiled, then cranked strength to 25 to prove the pipeline worked

decision: derived the moon framing distance from the camera field of view rather than a constant
why: 2.4x the apoapsis puts a moon at 22.6 degrees off axis, inside a 50 degree field by a hair and outside a narrower one
result: d = r / tan(fov/2 * 0.7); Moon ndcY 0.88 to 0.60, and Callisto and Phoebe also land in frame

decision: defaulted the clock to real time
why: the first thing a new viewer saw was Earth spinning once a second, which reads as a bug rather than as an 86,400x clock
result: verified 4.0 simulated seconds over 4 real seconds at startup

decision: extracted the engine to its own package rather than leaving it a folder inside the website
why: it was already dependency-pure, so it was a package pretending to be a folder, and native clients need it as the reference
result: purity is now structural: no website dependency, and no dom in lib so a DOM reference fails to compile

decision: four cwd-relative paths broke in the move and two of them would have failed silently
why: a directory walk that finds nothing passes every assertion it owns, which is an invariant quietly ceasing to be checked
result: all four now resolve from import.meta.url, and both walkers grew a count assertion

decision: generated the Standish tables, leap seconds, envelopes and display data into Swift rather than retyping them
why: four hundred numbers by hand is four hundred chances to misplace a digit, and a wrong element renders as a plausible wrong position
result: 123 lines of tables, 28 leap steps, 8 envelopes, all from the same parsed source the website reads

decision: built a cross-language drift gate: Swift emits residuals, TypeScript verifies them
why: a hand-port drifts, and a drifted physics engine does not throw, it puts a planet somewhere plausible and wrong
result: agreement to 1e-9 on all 8 planets and 64 epochs

decision: proved the drift gate bites by planting a 1e-7 error in the Swift
why: a gate that has never failed is not known to work, and this project has shipped a lint rule that silently did nothing
result: the Swift's own envelope tests still passed; the cross-check failed on all 8 planets

decision: gave the Sun a fixed render radius instead of the planets' exaggeration factor
why: at 1200x it came out 1.5 scene units and swallowed Mercury's orbit at 0.387 and Venus's at 0.723
result: verified on a booted simulator: Sun, Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars all legible on their orbits

decision: the device install failure was a deployment target, not signing
why: error 3002 after a clean compile reads as signing, but the phone runs iOS 26.6.1 and the app had defaulted to a 27.0 target
result: my own YAML slip nested deploymentTarget under settings instead of options, so Xcode fell back to the installed SDK

decision: pinned the SoBytes team in project.yml rather than a git-ignored xcconfig
why: a missing local override would let a build quietly sign as a personal team, and project.yml is the file XcodeGen actually reads
result: verified on the built app: TeamIdentifier FT97GD7996, application-identifier FT97GD7996.com.sobytes.solar

decision: dropped CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED NO
why: it makes simulator builds convenient and device installs impossible, surfacing as a build error rather than a signing one
result: simulator and device both build; 33 simulators usable again once the target came back to 17.0

decision: replaced the hard radius clamp with a square root of the size relative to Earth
why: a clamp of 0.045 to 0.10 is a 2.2-fold spread across bodies whose radii span 29-fold, so every planet came out the same size
result: spread is now 5.4-fold; the user spotted this before I did

decision: synced the real NASA textures into the bundle, downsized, chosen by the body contract
why: a flat tint is a placeholder, and picking textures by contract stops the phone and the website showing different imagery
result: 76.4 MB of source to 3.3 MB bundled, app 4.6 MB total

decision: wrote the master physics and mathematics contract, 645 lines
why: the user asked for the maths to glue everything together, grounded in the actual papers rather than folklore
result: each citation carries a confidence marker, since the search budget is exhausted and the project forbids presenting recall as verified

decision: made feature parity machine-readable and gated rather than a table
why: contracts exist to align platforms, and a feature shipped on web and never recorded is invisible from inside the web codebase
result: 21 features x 5 platforms; gate proved to bite by renaming a declared path
